title: Coherent convergence of localized finite filtered pages
statement: For any commutative R and any FilteredPageLocalizationData d [def-kun-filtered-page-localization-data], the image filtration in d.Hbar(n)(X) is finite for every localized object X. There are bounds N(X,n,a) at least 1 and isomorphisms gr^a d.Hbar(n)(X) to d.Sbar(X)_t^(a,n-a) for every t at least N. Both differentials vanish there. The comparisons are natural for every localized morphism on any common stationary page, and satisfy the normalized successor equation with iCycles, homology projection and the spectral-sequence successor isomorphism.

proof.text: Restriction to a filtration step commutes with its inclusion, by the defining factorization. Associated-graded maps commute with the cokernel projection, so their identity and composition laws follow by cancellation of this projection. Thus graded piece is a functor. Step restrictions of a filtered isomorphism are isomorphisms, by inclusion cancellation; this transfers finite endpoints.

For a finite filtered representative U, invert d.comparison.pageToImage followed by imageToGraded. The two stationary naturality squares in d give the naturality of this composite for every localized morphism between representatives. Its successor equation follows by composing successor_agreement and successor_graded_agreement. The normalized page model abutment specification identifies its finite filtration with the actual image filtration.

Every object of the chosen localization retains its finite filtered complex representative. Apply eH and eS at that representative to transport the graded comparison. Take the maximum of the stabilization bound in the normalized page model and d.bound. The page isomorphism transfers vanishing differentials. Conjugating a localized morphism by eH and eS gives exactly finiteFilteredDescendedMap, so the preceding naturality proves the desired square. Cycle-map naturality, homology-projection naturality, and the spectral-sequence morphism square transfer the successor equation.
